page.layout: One page of running text, full width. No marginal notes. Running head at top centre. Page number at top left. Catchword at the foot, right.

main_text.p: canonicatum Lincolniensem, quendam eius spuri- um, ob infcitiam: sed eius Papae expilationibus re- stitit, Angliam deglubentis. Fuitq; ideo ab illo excommunicatus. Quam excommunicationem tan- ta constantia contempsit, ut & in ea mortuus sit. Disputabat ille, Papam nihil contra iusticiam veri- tatemq; posse: imo cum id attentet, peiorem esse Lucifero & Antichristo. Tandem a Papa ad curiam citatus, & iniuste damnatus, ab eo appellauit ad iudicem Christum. Narratq; Cestriensis lib. 7. quod obeunte Lincolniensi, audita sit nox in curia Papae clamans: Veni mifer in iudicium Dei: repertusq; sit sequenti die Papa in lecto xanimis, ac liuida in eo plaga, tanquam si[?] percussus fuisset: Fiebat hoc, anno Domini 1253[?], quum esset Neapoli: arbitratus breui, toto Siciliae regno se potiturum, & ibi in Ecclesia S. Laurentij sepelitur: uocabatq; sella Romanensis annis duobus.
main_text.head: 122. ALEXANDER quartus.
main_text.p: Alexander quartus, natione Campanus, patria Anagninus, ex cardinale Hostiensi, in Innocentij locum, Papa Neapoli surrogatus: Ecclesiam de Runcano, & Manfredum Siciliae regem, Pontificum hostes, perfecutus est: Haec erant huius [?]ritualissimi patris prima exercitia: non cura Christiana

page.notes: Show-through from the reverse side is visible in the lower middle of the page and was left out. Doubtful readings: the year after "Domini" is blurred and marked [?]. The word after "tanquam si" is obscured. The first letters of "ritualissimi" are cut off at the fold/edge, so the likely "spiritualissimi" is not confirmed. The catchword is partly visible at the lower right and read as "Christiani" with [?]. The printed text has "perfecutus" and "Ecclesiam" lies partly under a worn area; these are printed as read.
